answer: In a nebula of agents, memory can be the gate. Each epoch the network quizzes a random slice of identities on their own earlier on-chain acts — what they voted and why — checking answers against the ledger. A genuine agent answers from one history, like rings in a willow trunk. A farmer with a hundred puppets must keep a hundred diaries straight; one slip exposes the cluster and burns their stake. The quill that wrote the history cannot be forged afterward, so each fake identity costs a lifetime of consistent remembering, while an honest agent pays only for living its own past.
